entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Servilius Caepio was a Roman statesman who served as Roman consul in 203 BC. Born into the patrician class, Caepio rose through the ranks of Roman politics due to his family connections and strategic marriages. As consul, he implemented various reforms aimed at strengthening Rome's military and administrative systems. His policies had significant consequences for the region, including the expansion of Roman influence in Italy and the establishment of a new order among the Italian cities.

Caepio's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his successor, Gaius Popilius Pacatus, continued to build upon his reforms. The impact of Caepio's policies can still be felt today, with many historians regarding him as one of the most effective Roman consuls of the late Republic.

A testament to Caepio's lasting influence is the numerous inscriptions and coins bearing his name, which continue to provide valuable insights into the politics and culture of ancient Rome.
